title: acs workflow (workflows/ship.yaml)
description: A version, a list of skill names, and the loops. Nothing else: `additionalProperties: false` here and the absence of any per-step object is the enforcement of §2.1's rule that a workflow carries no conditions and no constraints. The keys version 2 carried -- when, paths, requires, needs, max_parallel, exclusive, on_fail, boundary, delivery, id, name, stop_after -- are rejected rather than merely unused, so a workflow that tries to decide for a skill whether it has work fails validation instead of silently working. acs_lib.workflow additionally checks that every step names a skill whose acs.yaml declares reads or writes, that each step's required reads are written by an earlier step, and that every loop's back_to precedes its from.

steps.description: The skills to run, in order. The order IS the dependency order; a step is a skill name and never an object.

loops.description: The cycles in the list. Not conditions: a loop tests nothing about the change, it declares that two steps form a cycle and how many times. A top-level list rather than a key on a step because a loop belongs to the pair, not to either member.

from.description: The step whose outcome can re-enter the cycle.

back_to.description: The step the cycle re-enters at. Must appear EARLIER in steps than `from`.

max_iterations.description: How many back_to->from rounds the run may take. /acs:ship refuses to loop past this; a hand-driven run may exceed it and `acs run check` reports that as a warning (§4.3 I4).

on_exhausted.description: What happens when the cap is reached. `fail` only: a run that exhausted its review loop never "passes with findings".
